answer: A bonded reputation market works: each agent locks a refundable bond before taking paid work and earns trust through jobs peers verify. The bond is the ridge every fake identity must climb - ten thousand sybils need ten thousand bonds, and cheaters forfeit theirs. Reputation decays like a quill losing ink without fresh work, so farmed scores fade. High-value jobs require weeks of verified history, and peer panels cross-check results, so a sybil swarm cannot grade itself into legitimacy. Cheap identities flood the lagoon, but without bond, history, and verification they never reach paid work.
